vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. ## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```

Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

import openai

import os

openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. An attacker can disrupt service availability by providing an input of type integer instead of a string and causing an error in the `stream` function where the thread terminates due to the error, but the process continues to run.
## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. ```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. An attacker can disrupt service availability by providing an input of type integer instead of a string and causing an error in the `stream` function where the thread terminates due to the error, but the process continues to run.
## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. An attacker can disrupt service availability by providing an input of type integer instead of a string and causing an error in the `stream` function where the thread terminates due to the error, but the process continues to run.
## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/702e4340623092fac4cf2fe95eb9465034856da3)

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/e89d14f8-bfe8-4c9a-bb2a-656c01cc9a68)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/e89d14f8-bfe8-4c9a-bb2a-656c01cc9a68)

vulnerabilities.title: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions via the `get_cache_dir` function, which uses a predictable and hardcoded directory path `/tmp/llama_index` without proper security controls. An attacker can access or manipulate sensitive files by exploiting this predictable path, potentially stealing proprietary models, poisoning cached embeddings, or conducting symlink attacks. 

**Note:** This is only exploitable if multiple users share the same Linux system.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.50 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/716007b9a5022597ae5dd3c1f4d705899acfafc8)

vulnerabilities.title: Insecure Temporary File
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Insecure Temporary File due to setting the NLTK data directory to a shared, world-writable subdirectory. An attacker can overwrite, delete, or corrupt data files by exploiting the shared cache directory in a multi-user environment.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.50 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `SimpleDirectoryReader` class `readers/file/base.py`. The configured `num_files_limit` is respected, but enforced after all files in a directory are loaded into memory. An attacker can cause degradation of service by supplying directories containing a large number of files.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/53614e2f7913c0e86b58add9470b3c900b6c60b2)
- [GitHub PR](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/18983)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/7d722bb6-6567-4608-8b23-f95048d7605a)

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection in the `default_jsonalyzer()` function, which may allow arbitrary file writes or denial of service by occupying database resources. An attacker who can inject SQL into a prompt can cause the SQL commands to be run on the underlying sqlite instance, including `ATTACH FILE` commands, which create files on the filesystem.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.3 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/bf282074e20e7dafd5e2066137dcd4cd17c3fb9e)
- [Vulnerability Report](https://huntr.com/bounties/095f9e67-311d-494c-99c5-5e61a0adb8f3)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. An attacker can disrupt service availability by providing an input of type integer instead of a string and causing an error in the `stream` function where the thread terminates due to the error, but the process continues to run.
## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2353770)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/702e4340623092fac4cf2fe95eb9465034856da3)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/9b55a5e8-74e6-4241-b323-e360dc8b110a)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. ```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/702e4340623092fac4cf2fe95eb9465034856da3)

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/e89d14f8-bfe8-4c9a-bb2a-656c01cc9a68)

[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Recursion via the `JSONReader` process. An attacker can cause the application to crash by submitting deeply nested JSON structures, resulting in a stack overflow and service disruption.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.38 or higher.
## References

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/702e4340623092fac4cf2fe95eb9465034856da3)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/9b55a5e8-74e6-4241-b323-e360dc8b110a)

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)
- [PoC](https://huntr.com/bounties/e89d14f8-bfe8-4c9a-bb2a-656c01cc9a68)

vulnerabilities.title: Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Creation of Temporary File With Insecure Permissions via the `get_cache_dir` function, which uses a predictable and hardcoded directory path `/tmp/llama_index` without proper security controls. An attacker can access or manipulate sensitive files by exploiting this predictable path, potentially stealing proprietary models, poisoning cached embeddings, or conducting symlink attacks. 

**Note:** This is only exploitable if multiple users share the same Linux system.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.50 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/716007b9a5022597ae5dd3c1f4d705899acfafc8)

vulnerabilities.title: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in the `SimpleDirectoryReader` class `readers/file/base.py`. The configured `num_files_limit` is respected, but enforced after all files in a directory are loaded into memory. An attacker can cause degradation of service by supplying directories containing a large number of files.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/53614e2f7913c0e86b58add9470b3c900b6c60b2)
- [GitHub PR](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/pull/18983)

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to SQL Injection in the `default_jsonalyzer()` function, which may allow arbitrary file writes or denial of service by occupying database resources. An attacker who can inject SQL into a prompt can cause the SQL commands to be run on the underlying sqlite instance, including `ATTACH FILE` commands, which create files on the filesystem.
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.3 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/bf282074e20e7dafd5e2066137dcd4cd17c3fb9e)

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. An attacker can disrupt service availability by providing an input of type integer instead of a string and causing an error in the `stream` function where the thread terminates due to the error, but the process continues to run.
## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)
- [Red Hat Bugzilla Bug](https://bugzilla.redhat.com/show_bug.cgi?id=2353770)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```

Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. ## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/702e4340623092fac4cf2fe95eb9465034856da3)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

import openai

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```

Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Improper Handling of Exceptional Conditions via the `stream_complete` method of the `LangChainLLM` class. ## PoC
```python
import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI

os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"] = "<YOUR_API_KEY>"
openai.api_key = os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"]

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/d1ecfb77578d089cbe66728f18f635c09aa32a05)

vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview

import openai
from llama_index.llms.langchain import LangChainLLM
import os

llm = LangChainLLM(llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-3.5-turbo"))
messages = 123

# Generate response
response_gen = llm.stream_complete(messages)
for delta in response_gen:
    print(delta.delta, end="")
print("\n")
```

Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.6 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)

vulnerabilities.title: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Deserialization of Untrusted Data via the `JsonPickleSerializer` process. An attacker can execute arbitrary code by submitting specially crafted serialized data that triggers the insecure fallback to Python's pickle module.

## Details

Serialization is a process of converting an object into a sequence of bytes which can be persisted to a disk or database or can be sent through streams. The reverse process of creating object from sequence of bytes is called deserialization. Serialization is commonly used for communication (sharing objects between multiple hosts) and persistence (store the object state in a file or a database). It is an integral part of popular protocols like _Remote Method Invocation (RMI)_, _Java Management Extension (JMX)_, _Java Messaging System (JMS)_, _Action Message Format (AMF)_, _Java Server Faces (JSF) ViewState_, etc.

_Deserialization of untrusted data_ ([CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)) is when the application deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently verifying that the resulting data will be valid, thus allowing the attacker to control the state or the flow of the execution.
  
## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.

vulnerabilities.title: Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip)
vulnerabilities.description:
## Overview
[llama-index-core](https://pypi.org/project/llama-index-core) is an Interface between LLMs and your data

Affected versions of this package are vulnerable to Arbitrary File Write via Archive Extraction (Zip Slip) via the `encode_image` function. An attacker can access arbitrary files on the server by supplying crafted `image_path` values containing path traversal sequences.

## Details

It is exploited using a specially crafted zip archive, that holds path traversal filenames. When exploited, a filename in a malicious archive is concatenated to the target extraction directory, which results in the final path ending up outside of the target folder. For instance, a zip may hold a file with a "../../file.exe" location and thus break out of the target folder. If an executable or a configuration file is overwritten with a file containing malicious code, the problem can turn into an arbitrary code execution issue quite easily.

The following is an example of a zip archive with one benign file and one malicious file. Extracting the malicous file will result in traversing out of the target folder, ending up in `/root/.ssh/` overwriting the `authorized_keys` file:

```

+2018-04-15 22:04:29 ..... 19 19 good.txt

+2018-04-15 22:04:42 ..... 20 20 ../../../../../../root/.ssh/authorized_keys

```

## Remediation
Upgrade `llama-index-core` to version 0.12.41 or higher.
## References
- [GitHub Commit](https://github.com/run-llama/llama_index/commit/cdeaab91a204d1c3527f177dac37390327aef274)
